headline: France 24h walkout ~24 ports, Italy nationwide ports strike, Greek ferries disrupted
dek: The coordinated dockworkers action is underway today: France's CGT called a 24-hour walkout across ~24 ports, predicting as much as 95% of national port activity could be halted; Italy registered a nationwide 24-hour ports strike coinciding with a general strike; Greek seafarers' unions called…
sources: Splash247 (day-of mobilisation report, Oct 30); Reuters Oct 29 (underlying call: 113 ports, 22 countries, 25+ unions)
fault_line: Blocking war cargo, or blocking ordinary people? Greek ferries stay docked while the action targets arms shipments -- the civilian cost is the argument.

sections.what_happened: The coordinated dockworkers action is underway today: France's CGT called a 24-hour walkout across ~24 ports, predicting as much as 95% of national port activity could be halted; Italy registered a nationwide 24-hour ports strike coinciding with a general strike; Greek seafarers' unions called 24-hour stoppages disrupting ferries at Piraeus, Rafina, Lavrio, Patras and Igoumenitsa (Piraeus dockworkers' own stoppage 0800-1100 GMT = 12:00-15:00 ). Organisers estimate ~40,000 containers potentially delayed and workers handling ~40% of Mediterranean container traffic. Genoa's port authority still expects only limited disruption. NO verified tally of delayed containers, halted ships or lost freight was retrieved by 13:00 -- the 40,000 / 95% / $2bn figures remain organiser/union estimates, not counted disruption.
sections.what_verified: Underlying call: Reuters (T1) Oct 29. Day-of details: Splash247 carries NO declared tier in the registry and does not count toward corroboration. Sig 2, so the sig>=3 gate does not apply; PASS is for 'action underway, impact uncounted' framing only.
sections.what_disputed: Genoa port spokesman (via Reuters) expects limited impact -- the mobilisation's scale does not equal its disruption. Some ports are holding demonstrations rather than stopping cargo (Splash247). No port authority or carrier tally retrieved.
sections.why_matters: Shipping-war labour beat: 113 ports, day of action, ferries docked in Greece and a 95%-halt claim in France -- but still no counted container, ship or dollar of actual disruption.
sections.context: Background: DAY-OF UPDATE to 0400-06 -- Global dockworkers action underway Fri Oct 30: France 24h walkout ~24 ports, Italy nationwide ports strike, Greek ferries disrupted; no verified disruption tally yet

totw_analysis: Our read: Shipping-war labour beat: 113 ports, day of action, ferries docked in Greece and a 95%-halt claim in France -- but still no counted container, ship or dollar of actual disruption. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Blocking war cargo, or blocking ordinary people? Greek ferries stay docked while the action targets arms shipments -- the civilian cost is the argument.
